body.prompt: Winter evening in 2011 in a narrow Myeongdong alley in Seoul: a long line of people in winter coats waiting outside a small spicy braised chicken restaurant with a glowing sign, breath visible in the cold air, a mother and her teenage daughter seen from behind walking past and looking at the line, neon reflections on the wet pavement.

Black-and-white documentary photograph style, early 1960s Seoul Namdaemun market alley: a long line of poorly dressed people holding tin bowls waiting at a street stall where porridge steams from a huge pot, crowded wooden stalls, faded archival film grain.

A food research lab tasting table seen from above: many white plates of glossy red-coated chicken pieces and small sauce bowls, glasses of milk and water, notebooks with handwritten notes, a few tired hands holding forks, bright clinical light.

A clean Scandinavian supermarket aisle with instant noodle shelves: one eye-level shelf section stands conspicuously empty with a small white notice card taped to the shelf edge, colorful packages on either side with unreadable labels, soft Nordic daylight.
